beats: A whole family in a German casino town was waiting for Granny to die.
The broke General needed her fortune to marry a French beauty called Blanche.
Then Granny arrived, very much alive, carried in her armchair!
This is The Gambler, by Fyodor Dostoyevsky.
She went straight to the roulette table and bet on zero.
Zero hit, and then hit again!
Two days later, she'd lost nearly a hundred thousand roubles.
Then the family's tutor sat down, and red came up again and again.
He broke the bank: two hundred thousand francs!
Blanche took him to Paris, and in three weeks the money was gone.
Months later, Granny finally died, and the General got his inheritance.
Then he died of a stroke, and his new wife, Blanche, kept every franc!
The tutor ended up in debtors' prison, then working as a footman.
The author, a gambler himself, dictated this book in twenty-six days to beat a deadline.
The tutor got ten gold coins from a friend, and started waiting all over again.
